label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_battery.mdl, models/w_squeak.mdl, models/w_adrenaline.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: It reads as a wrench: a long handle, a head block, an adjusting ring and two parallel jaws, as TOP and BELOW show. But the head is three separate plain boxes rather than one jaw piece. The jaws are flat rectangular bars with square ends and no hooked upper jaw, so in FRONT-LEFT and BACK-RIGHT the outline looks more like a forked bracket than a pipe wrench.

M2.reason: It measures 20.6 long against the 18 asked, 14.6% over, which is inside the 15% allowed. Width (9.6) and thickness (2.9) are plausible for a pipe wrench's jaw and handle.

M3.reason: The handle, the head, the adjusting ring (the brown ring between the jaws) and two jaws are all there. The brief's 'heavy toothed jaw' has no teeth in any view, and the jaws are thin blocks rather than heavy ones. The two jaws also meet the head as loose boxes, with no frame or shank joining them.

M4.reason: The red-painted handle with bare grey patches matches the brief. The jaw blocks are a pale bluish-white, almost untextured, and read as clean aluminium or plastic rather than iron (FRONT-RIGHT, in-hand.png). The handle's red is very saturated, and the dark streak along it makes it look glassy in in-hand.png and in LEFT.

M5.reason: The handle has the wear to bare iron, as dark grey patches in first-person.png and attack.png. There are no jaw teeth, the adjusting ring has no knurling, and the jaws have no grime or wear. Their faces are flat pale fills with one bevel shade.

M6.reason: In lineup.png the wrench is D, and it stands out at once beside A to C: a few flat untextured boxes where the game's items carry painted detail. In first-person.png the game's crowbar is cleaner and more finished. The blocky white jaws would not pass as Valve's work.

M7.reason: The w_ model lies flat and level (FRONT, LEFT, RIGHT and BACK show it horizontal at one height), the head is at one end, and nothing sits tilted or sunk.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors, and at 156 triangles it is small for a weapon of this size. No part is inside out or open in any view, and the jaws touch the ring and head.

W1.reason: It is held the same way round, head up and handle running down out of the frame, and it follows the swing through attack frames 0 to 10, coming back to rest. But it leans much further left and sits higher than the crowbar. The head nearly touches the top edge of the frame, and the wrench fills more of the view, so it does not sit where the crowbar sits.
